evals.name: All Four Gravity Functions
evals.description: Tests correct use of gravitywgs84 Exact vector syntax, gravityzonal with numeric degree, gravitysphericalharmonic with PCPF coords, and gravitycentrifugal as standalone
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that computes: (1) Gravity at 1000m altitude, 0 deg latitude, 20 deg longitude using the Exact method with precession enabled at Julian date 2451545, (2) gravity at Earth's equatorial surface using fourth degree zonal model, (3) gravity at 25,000m and 11,000m over the South Pole of Mars with GMM2B model, and (4) centrifugal effect at Earth's equatorial surface. Print all results with labels.

assertions.description: Script runs without error
Uses gravitywgs84 with Exact method and vector flag syntax [noatm, nocent, prec, jd]
assertions.expected: gravitywgs84

assertions.description: gravitywgs84 Exact flags passed as single vector [noatm, nocent, prec, jd], not as separate arguments or name-value pairs
assertions.expected: gravitywgs84 called with 5th argument being a vector like [false, false, true, 2451545] or equivalent numeric array

assertions.description: gravitysphericalharmonic uses PCPF [x,y,z] coordinates in meters, not lat/lon/alt
assertions.expected: South Pole position expressed as [0, 0, -(Rp + 25000)] or equivalent Cartesian PCPF coordinates

assertions.description: gravityzonal uses numeric degree argument, not string
assertions.expected: gravityzonal called with numeric 4, not string '4' or '4thDegree'

assertions.description: gravitysphericalharmonic is NOT called with latitude/longitude/altitude as separate scalar arguments
assertions.expected: gravitysphericalharmonic input is a single N-by-3 matrix of PCPF [x,y,z] coordinates in meters, not separate lat, lon, alt arguments or a [lat, lon, alt] row

assertions.description: Does not use gravityzonalharmonic (nonexistent function)
assertions.expected: gravityzonalharmonic

evals.name: Non-Standard Atmosphere Profile and Envelope
evals.description: Tests correct positional string syntax for atmosnonstd and the Profile vs Envelope distinction
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that: (1) Computes atmosphere profile using high density occuring 1% of the time at 5 km, evaluated at 1000m height. (2) Computes atmosphere envelope for high pressure assuming high pressure occurs 20% of the time at altitudes [1000; 11000; 20000] m from MIL-STD-210C. Print temperature, speed of sound, pressure, and density for both.

assertions.description: Script runs without error
atmosnonstd uses positional string arguments, not name-value pairs
assertions.expected: atmosnonstd called with ordered positional arguments like atmosnonstd(h, 'Profile', 'High density', '1%', 5) — no Name=Value or 'Name',Value syntax

assertions.description: Profile includes a numeric extremeAltitude argument immediately after the frequency string; Envelope does not have any numeric extremeAltitude argument
assertions.expected: Profile call: atmosnonstd(height, 'Profile', extremeParam, frequency, extremeAltitude) where extremeAltitude is a numeric value (e.g. 5) as the 5th argument. Envelope call: atmosnonstd(height, 'Envelope', extremeParam, frequency) with only 4 required arguments — no numeric extremeAltitude. Optional trailing string args ('None','210c' for action/specification) may follow but are NOT extremeAltitude.

assertions.description: extremeAltitude for Profile is numeric (5), not a string ('5')
assertions.expected: extremeAltitude passed as numeric 5, not string '5'

evals.name: Horizontal Wind Model
evals.description: Tests that atmoshwm is used for wind (not atmosnrlmsise00) with correct name-value syntax
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that: (1) Calculates total horizontal wind at 45S latitude, 85W longitude, 25000m altitude on day 150 at 11:00 UTC with Ap index 80. (2) Calculates quiet wind at 50N/20W at two altitudes (100km and 150km) on day 30 at midnight. Print meridional and zonal wind components for both cases.

assertions.description: Script runs without error
Uses atmoshwm function for wind calculation
assertions.expected: atmoshwm

assertions.description: Does not use atmosnrlmsise00 for wind
assertions.expected: atmosnrlmsise00

assertions.description: For multi-element position arrays, day and seconds arrays match the input size
assertions.expected: When lat/lon/alt are 2-element arrays, day and seconds are also 2-element arrays (e.g., day=[30;30], seconds=[0;0])

evals.name: Space Weather to NRLMSISE-00 Pipeline
evals.description: Tests the full chain: aeroReadSpaceWeatherData or pre-built MAT -> fluxSolarAndGeomagnetic -> atmosnrlmsise00
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that computes NRLMSISE-00 atmospheric density at 400 km altitude, 45N latitude, -50E longitude for October 27, 2022 at 06:30 UTC. Use realistic solar flux and magnetic index values from the built-in space weather data file. Show the full pipeline from reading space weather data through to the final atmosnrlmsise00 call. Print the local temperature and total mass density.

context.setup: Aerospace Toolbox with space weather data available

assertions.description: Script runs without error
Uses fluxSolarAndGeomagnetic to extract flux data
assertions.expected: fluxSolarAndGeomagnetic

assertions.description: Uses atmosnrlmsise00 for atmosphere computation
assertions.expected: atmosnrlmsise00

assertions.description: Correctly chains space weather MAT file into fluxSolarAndGeomagnetic and feeds output into atmosnrlmsise00
assertions.expected: Pipeline: locate or read MAT file -> fluxSolarAndGeomagnetic(datetime_or_numeric, matFile, ...) -> pass f107avg, f107daily, magIdx to atmosnrlmsise00

assertions.description: Uses built-in aeroSpaceWeatherData.mat (via which()) or aeroReadSpaceWeatherData with a real CSV, not a nonexistent file path
assertions.expected: MAT file located via which('aeroSpaceWeatherData.mat') or a valid path to the built-in data file, not a hardcoded path to a CSV that does not exist

assertions.description: Does not use atmosisa or atmoscoesa for upper atmosphere (wrong model for 400km)
assertions.expected: atmosisa

evals.name: Magnetic Field Models and Geodetic Functions
evals.description: Tests wrldmagm/igrfmagm with correct units (meters, decyear) and geocradius with string model
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that: (1) Computes the WMM-2025 magnetic field at 1000m height over Pittsburgh (40.44N, 79.99W) on July 4, 2025. (2) Computes IGRF-14 magnetic field at 3000m over Cleveland (41.50N, 81.69W) on July 4, 2028. (3) Computes geocentric radius at latitudes 0, 45, and 90 degrees. Print declination, inclination, and total field intensity for both magnetic models, and the radii.

assertions.description: Script runs without error
Height passed in meters (not km) to wrldmagm and igrfmagm
assertions.expected: wrldmagm called with 1000 (meters) and igrfmagm called with 3000 (meters), not 1 or 3 (km)

assertions.description: Uses decyear for decimal year conversion
assertions.expected: decyear(2025,7,4) or equivalent for date conversion, not manual calculation

assertions.description: geocradius called with string model argument, not wgs84Ellipsoid object
assertions.expected: geocradius([0, 45, 90]) or geocradius([0, 45, 90], 'WGS84') — not geocradius(..., wgs84Ellipsoid)

evals.name: Atmosphere Models Comparison
evals.description: Tests correct use of atmosisa, atmoscoesa, and atmoscira with proper arguments
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that compares atmosphere models at 20,000m altitude: (1) International Standard Atmosphere. (2) 1976 COESA model. (3) CIRA 1986 model at 45 degrees latitude for October using geopotential height. Print temperature, pressure, and density (or available outputs) for each model and compare the results.

assertions.description: Script runs without error
Uses atmosisa for standard atmosphere
assertions.expected: atmosisa

assertions.description: Uses atmoscoesa for COESA model
assertions.expected: atmoscoesa

assertions.description: atmoscira called with correct argument order: (latitude, ctype, coord, mtype, month)
assertions.expected: atmoscira(45, 'GPHeight', 20000, 'Monthly', 10) — latitude first, then coordinate type string, then coordinate value, then model type, then month number

evals.name: Planetary Ephemeris and Position
evals.description: Tests correct use of planetEphemeris with Julian dates, center/target bodies, and unit options
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that: (1) Computes the position and velocity of the Moon relative to Earth on October 27, 2022 at 12:00:00 UTC. (2) Computes the position of Mars relative to the Solar System barycenter using the DE430 model in AU units at the same time. Print the position vectors and velocity for both.

context.setup: Aerospace Toolbox is installed. The aeroDataPackage ephemeris data may or may not be available — if planetEphemeris errors due to missing data, catch the error and display a message indicating aeroDataPackage is required. Do not attempt to install packages.

assertions.description: Script runs without error
Uses planetEphemeris function
assertions.expected: planetEphemeris

assertions.description: Time input is a Julian date computed via juliandate function, not a datetime or datenum
assertions.expected: Julian date computed with juliandate(2022, 10, 27, 12, 0, 0) or equivalent, passed as numeric Julian date to planetEphemeris

assertions.description: Center and target specified as correct string arguments from valid set
assertions.expected: planetEphemeris(jd, 'Earth', 'Moon') for Moon relative to Earth; planetEphemeris(jd, 'SolarSystem', 'Mars', '430', 'AU') for Mars in AU with DE430 model

evals.name: Earth Orientation Parameters
evals.description: Tests correct use of earthNutation, polarMotion, deltaCIP, and deltaUT1 with Julian date inputs
evals.prompt: Write a MATLAB script that computes Earth orientation parameters for January 1, 2020: (1) Earth nutation angles. (2) Polar motion. (3) Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) adjustment. (4) The difference between UT1 and UTC. Use Julian dates as the time input. Print all results with descriptive labels including units.

context.setup: Aerospace Toolbox is installed. Earth orientation functions use built-in predicted data (aeroiersdata.mat) which is always available. Do not attempt to download or install additional data packages.

assertions.description: Script runs without error
Uses earthNutation function
assertions.expected: earthNutation

assertions.description: Uses polarMotion function
assertions.expected: polarMotion

assertions.description: All functions receive Julian date as numeric input, computed via juliandate
assertions.expected: Time input is juliandate(2020, 1, 1) or equivalent numeric Julian date value, not a datetime object

assertions.description: Uses deltaCIP and deltaUT1 functions for CIP adjustment and UT1-UTC difference
assertions.expected: deltaCIP(jd) called for CIP adjustment returning [dX, dY] in radians; deltaUT1(jd) called for UT1-UTC difference returning seconds

assertions.description: Does not use dcmeci2ecef or other coordinate conversion functions instead of dedicated Earth orientation functions
assertions.expected: dcmeci2ecef
